ai.title: Remove native tool use, switch to tag-based streaming
ai.summary: Native Anthropic tool use removed from backend. promptClaudeStream now yields strings only; tool call yields commented out. processStreamWithFiles replaced by generic processStreamWithTags parsing XML-like tags with attributes. DEFAULT_TOOLS imports and tools parameters stripped from request-files-prompt, generate-knowledge-files, and main-prompt. stop_sequences: [] added to claude.ts API call.

eli5.text: The coding assistant no longer uses its old built-in way of calling helper tools during conversations. Instead of automatically running code or searching files through a special tool interface, it now reads and responds to simple text tags you include in your requests (like marking sections with tags the system looks for). If you were using a workflow that depended on automatic tool actions from the assistant, those will stop working; you'd need to include tag-based markers in your prompts instead. This change is live today across the core assistant and file-generation features.

ai.title: Log npm version check result in websocket-action.ts
ai.summary: Added `console.log` in `onCheckNpmVersion` to log `clientVersion` and `latestVersion` alongside `isUpToDate` status. Provides visibility into version mismatch detection during websocket checks. Scope limited to `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant, it now quietly records whether your installed version matches the newest one while checking for updates over the websocket connection. This is a behind-the-scenes logging tweak for the maintenance team, so it doesn't change anything you see or do. The only noticeable effect is a new line in the server logs showing the version numbers during that health check. It's live today as part of the tool's standard maintenance.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.65
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.65 in backend/package.json and npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: The software's two main components were both quietly moved forward to a new release number, essentially refreshing the versioned package that the backend and desktop app report as their current build. You won't notice anything different in day-to-day use because this only stamps a new release number onto existing code rather than changing how anything works. Live today for anyone who checks their installed version numbers.

ai.title: Add colon to Manicode prompt in CLI
ai.summary: The `Manicode` prompt in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` now includes a trailing colon (`Manicode:`). This change affects the CLI's visual output when waiting for user input. No functional logic or user-facing behavior changes occur beyond this formatting adjustment.

eli5.text: You'll now see a colon after 'Manicode' when the assistant waits for you to type something in the command-line tool (the text-only version). Previously it showed just 'Manicode ' with a space; now it shows 'Manicode: ' like a normal prompt. This is purely a tiny visual tweak in the program's text display, affecting only how the input line looks while nothing else functionally changed.

ai.title: Suppress deadConnectionCleaner errors
ai.summary: Commented out `console.error` in `deadConnectionCleaner` catch block in `backend/src/websockets/server.ts`. Prevents noisy logs during client termination errors. Refactored `SWITCHBOARD.getClient(ws)` into a local `client` variable for readability.

eli5.text: When a connection to the service gets dropped unexpectedly, the system used to log a noticeable error message in the logs. That logging has been turned off, so those specific error messages will no longer appear during connection cleanup. The system will still detect and disconnect stale connections the same way; you just won't see those error messages anymore if you look at the logs.

ai.title: Limit file tree scan to 10k files
ai.summary: getProjectFileTree now uses breadth-first search with a maxFiles limit (default 10,000) to prevent excessive scanning. Special handling added for home directory scans (max 1000 files, ignores dotfiles). New DirectoryNode type introduced in util/file.ts for tree construction.

eli5.text: When the assistant scans your project's folders to build a file list, it now stops automatically after counting 10,000 items. If you direct it at a very large directory (like your computer's main home folder), it caps the scan at 1,000 items and skips hidden files. You'll notice the file list just ends sooner in those cases, the change is live today for any scan that would otherwise try to crawl a huge folder tree.

ai.title: Auto-update Manicode via npm registry check
ai.summary: Replaced backend WebSocket version check with client-side auto-update in `update-manicode.ts`. Scrape npm registry for latest version, compare semver, and run global install via detected package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm/bun). Removed `check-npm-version` and `npm-version-status` actions from `common/src/actions.ts` and `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`. `scripts/bump-version.ts` now only increments `npm-app` version.

eli5.text: Manicode now checks for new versions directly through your web browser connection instead of asking a separate server each time you start it. When a newer version is available, it automatically updates itself using whatever package manager you already use (npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun), and it shows a green message telling you the update succeeded. If the version check fails or you're offline, the tool still starts normally without waiting for it.

ai.title: update-manicode error log drops stack trace
ai.summary: updateManicode error handler in npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts now logs static string 'Failed to update Manicode.' instead of concatenating error object. Removes stack trace and error message details from console output. Scope limited to single catch block in update flow.

eli5.text: When the assistant tried to update its helper tool and that update process hit an unexpected error, it used to print a detailed technical message showing exactly what went wrong, including where the problem happened in the code. Now it just prints a simple message saying the update failed, without any of those extra details. This only affects anyone who manually checked the program's diagnostic output while the update was running.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.66
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.66 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The team marked a new numbered release of their internal assistant tool, moving the version label forward to keep track of what ships. The version bump itself only changes a label, but installing this version pulls in a collection of smaller fixes and changes that shipped between the previous two releases (Sept 21 - 24), including a switch from native tool calls to a simpler tag-based streaming method, a cap that stops the project file scan after 10,000 files, and client-side auto-updating through the npm registry. If you install or update today, you get that combined set of changes rather than a single new capability.
